clips.title: The story
paras: This sacred rite marks a tauren shaman's spiritual attunement to the element of earth. By drinking an Earth Sapta at a holy rock east of Camp Narache, initiates peer beyond physical senses to commune directly with a Minor Manifestation of Earth.

A sapta is a carefully concocted ceremonial potion crafted by shamanic elders to bind an initiate's mortal spirit directly to a primal element. Prepared with ancestral magic, only a select few among the tauren preserve the secrets of its brewing. When imbibed at a designated sacred site, the draught expands the imbiber's mind, piercing the veil between the physical realm and the spiritual plane so the elements can be witnessed in their raw form.

East of Camp Narache stands Kodo Rock, a looming stone pillar that serves as a holy sanctuary. Consuming the sapta here reveals the Minor Manifestation of Earth awaiting the pilgrim. Unlike the volatile, fiery, or raging aspects of nature encountered later along the shaman's path, the spirit of earth asks only that the initiate approach in quiet humility, granting the mountain's enduring strength and the plains' calm patience to all who honor the land.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: A sapta is a drink created to bind our spirits to the elements. Fused with magic, the potion will allow the open minded to see the elements as no one has seen them before. Your spirit will forever be tied to the element the sapta was created for, and only a select few of our kind know the secrets of its creation.
The sapta is always imbibed in a holy place, and never anywhere else.
Seek out the shaman shrine to the east of here and drink of the sapta.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Ah... Friend... Pleased is the earth to have you here.
Bound together in body and spirit, you will go forward knowing that the mountains are your strength; the plains, your patience; and the world itself your essence.

Standing before the earth humbly is all that is required of you for you to pass this rite. But the others are not as passive. They may be chaotic and often violent, but such is the nature of the elements. Dual natures opposing one another, you must come to learn these things intricately.
